surprises.description: SNDL's cannabis operations deteriorated much more sharply than the preview's roughly C$33 million revenue base suggested: revenue was C$27.0 million, down 27.7% year over year. The preview described the prior-quarter decline as 10.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cannabis operations net revenue fell 27.7% to $27.0 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cannabis Operations — C$32.2M, −10.1% YoY”; the preview also referred to a “~C$33M revenue base.”

surprises.description: Instead of the partial margin recovery the preview expected, cannabis operations posted a negative 6% gross margin. The preview's base case was 8–12%, and it identified a margin below 5% as a key downside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cannabis operations net revenue fell 27.7% to $27.0 million with a negative 6% gross margin”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Cannabis Ops GM ~8–12% (partial Jeeter recovery)”; “still below 5% = the ‘fixable’ claim loses credibility.”

surprises.description: SNDL reported a C$48.3 million operating loss, far worse than the preview's roughly C$6 million loss expectation, because it recorded a C$52 million noncash goodwill impairment tied to cannabis operations. Adjusted operating income was nevertheless positive at C$5.2 million, so the reported loss was heavily affected by the impairment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported an operating loss of $48.3 million, reflecting a $52 million noncash goodwill impairment tied to cannabis operations”; “Adjusted operating income returned to positive territory at $5.2 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's Q3 base table estimated “Operating income (C$M) … ~(6).”

surprises.description: The cannabis weakness prompted a strategic review, including potential asset divestitures, alongside an exit from unprofitable domestic dried flower and a workforce cut of more than 30% at Kelowna. That is a more consequential retreat than the preview's framing of the Jeeter margin problem as fixable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The results] prompt[ed] a strategic review including potential asset divestitures after the company exited the unprofitable domestic dried flower category and cut over 30% of its Kelowna facility workforce.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview quoted management calling the margin shortfall “fixable” and said the bull case required that “Jeeter lines reach designed throughput and absorb overhead.”

surprises.description: Liquor Retail same-store sales fell 6%, worse than the preview's expectation of a decline better than 4%. Its record 27% gross margin was a positive offset, but did not prevent the sales-comp miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liquor Retail achieved a record 27.0% gross margin despite a 6% same-store sales decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for: GM ≥26% (vs. 25.1% in Q2) and a decline rate better than −4%.”

surprises.description: The Ontario AGCO resolution creates a large reported-revenue reduction when the franchise operations are deconsolidated: about $105 million, despite only about $2 million of operating income being removed. The preview did not flag this resolution or its accounting impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The anticipated resolution of the Ontario AGCO regulatory matter, requiring a $200,000 penalty and ~$30 million of third-party financing, would deconsolidate Ontario franchise operations, cutting reported net revenue by ~$105 million but only ~$2 million of operating income.”

surprises.description: Despite record free cash flow, cash fell by $50.7 million, mainly because SNDL contributed $60.8 million to equity-accounted investees and spent $10 million on repurchases. The preview highlighted the record cash flow and Q2 cash balance but did not anticipate this scale of quarterly cash deployment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash declined by $50.7 million in the quarter, primarily due to $60.8 million of capital contributions to equity-accounted investees and $10 million of share repurchases.”

surprises.description: SNDL raised its stake in Parallel's take-back debt from 39.4% to 69.4% by buying additional debt at 75% of face value. The preview noted the increase in SNDL's indirect equity ownership to about 92%, but did not anticipate this additional debt acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[SNDL] raised its stake in Parallel's take-back debt from 39.4% to 69.4% by acquiring additional debt at 75% of face value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said SNDL had “raised its indirect economic interest from ~67% to ~92%”; it did not mention an increase in the take-back debt stake.

surprises.description: SNDL's formal substantial issuer bid was expected after the release, but the reported update was a potential bid of up to $50 million rather than a clearly formalized offer with launch mechanics. The maximum price matches the preview's stated USD 1.35 ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[SNDL] announced a potential substantial issuer bid of up to $50 million at a price not exceeding USD 1.35 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “SIB of up to C$50M at a max C$1.92 (US$1.35) … is expected to launch formally after this earnings release.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in above the preview's base estimate and declined less year over year than expected: C$238 million and down 2.5%, versus a base of about C$232 million and an expected decline of about 5%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case was “Net revenue (C$) … ~C$232M (−5% YoY)”; its consensus conversion was approximately C$229 million.

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin was 24.3%, below the preview's roughly 25.0% expectation, and gross profit fell 9.8%. This was a weaker margin result despite the better-than-expected revenue decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit fell 9.8% to $57.9 million and gross margin contracted 2 percentage points to 24.3% due to weak cannabis operations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's Q3 base table estimated “Gross margin … ~25.0%.”

surprises.description: Cannabis Retail posted record revenue of $85.6 million and a 27.0% gross margin, up from the preview's Q2 reference of C$83.2 million and 26.4%. That was somewhat better than the preview's expectation of a continuing bright spot.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cannabis Retail reached $85.6 million net revenue with 27.0% gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Cannabis Retail as “the one bright spot,” citing Q2 revenue of “C$83.2M” and gross margin of “26.4%, +improving.”
